habitat_value: Moderate to high spawning capability for resident and anadromous fish; low rearing (poor habitat diversity, low instream cover). Bed predominantly small gravels; 80% glide/20% riffle.
upstream_fish: Chinook spawning confirmed (Reaches 1,3,5,6,11); bull trout sampled (Reaches 1-3); rainbow trout present in mainstem
recommendation: Create scour pools in Reaches 1,2 & 3; boulder & debris placements in Reaches 1,2 & 3 (Sec 6.5)
notes: West channel surveyed; east channel ('Lower Summit Creek') not surveyed. Potential side-channel development site identified (also Reaches 6 and 11). Sec 6.5 priority is restoration priority, not crossing/barrier priority. No coords or PSCIS id printed in report.

habitat_value: Moderate spawning (limited by high gravel mobility, absence of adult holding areas, high fines); moderate to high rearing (back-channel areas), limited by small bed material and low instream cover.
upstream_fish: Bull trout sampled (Reaches 1-3); chinook and rainbow present in mainstem
recommendation: Create scour pools in Reaches 1,2 & 3; boulder & debris placements in Reaches 1,2 & 3 (Sec 6.5)
notes: Sec 6.5 restoration priority (not a crossing/barrier priority).

barrier: Series of major debris jams in the lower section of the reach could impede upstream fish passage under some flow conditions
habitat_value: Low to moderate spawning (gravel quality rated low in 10 of 22 detailed units); moderate to high rearing (high riffle + side-channel area, more cobble).
upstream_fish: Chinook spawning and juvenile chinook rearing confirmed; bull trout sampled (Reaches 1-3); rainbow present
recommendation: Create scour pools in Reaches 1,2 & 3; boulder & debris placements in Reaches 1,2 & 3 (Sec 6.5)
notes: Reaches 4 and 5 not surveyed due to foot-access problems (combined length 16.8 km). Slump locations shown on Map 93H-023.

habitat_value: Spawning limited by low pool/holding frequency and fair gravel quality (low for 8 of 17 detailed units); low to moderate rearing (cobble + LWD cover, some off-channel), limited by low pool frequency/diversity.
upstream_fish: Chinook spawning confirmed in this reach
notes: Monkton and Pleasant Valley creeks enter in this reach; extensive placer mining near Pleasant Valley confluence. Potential side-channel development site.

habitat_value: Spawning limited by low occurrence of holding pools and fair gravel quality; rearing limited by moderate habitat diversity and absence of cobble cover.
notes: Two bridge crossings on the creek (logging road; one at downstream reach boundary, one ~500 m below upper boundary). Inactive placer mine on right bank.

habitat_value: Spawning highest in gravel riffle sections adjacent to pools; low to moderate rearing, limited by low side-channel habitat, minimal debris cover and lack of overhanging bank vegetation.
notes: Right-bank unnamed tributary flows through a culvert and down a steep embankment - 'there is no fish access into this creek' (tributary, not mainstem). Mainline logging-road bridge at lower reach boundary identified as a point source for sediment erosion.

habitat_value: Spawning for resident fish may be limited by high cobble content; deep pools provide good adult holding habitat; rearing limited by low instream debris and absence of off-channel habitat (cobble/boulder cover important).
notes: No bridge crossings in this reach.

habitat_value: Low to moderate spawning (limited by poor gravel quality); rearing limited by lack of off-channel habitat and low instream debris.
notes: Left-bank tributary flows through a culvert at the 3100 road. Placer mining throughout most of reach. One bridge crossing near upper reach boundary.

habitat_value: Spawning limited by low riffle occurrence (not limited by gravel availability or adult holding); rearing supported by abundant off-channel/point bars but limited by low riffle frequency, absence of cobble cover, low debris.
upstream_fish: Chinook spawning confirmed; upstream limit of chinook distribution (found up to Reach 11); rainbow present
recommendation: Re-plant cleared riparian areas in Reaches 11 & 13 (Sec 6.5, low/medium restoration priority)
notes: Large placer mine near upper end (~500 m of channel in-filled by mining). Mainline logging-road bridge in mid-section. Potential side-channel development site.

barrier: Some sections of the 306 m long cascade located in the upstream section of the reach may be barriers to upstream fish migration under some flow conditions
habitat_value: No significant spawning capability (high gradient, large bed material); rearing highest in lower cobble riffle sections but limited by low organic debris and absence of side-channel habitat.
upstream_fish: Chinook salmon unlikely in Reach 12 and upstream due to presence of migration obstructions in Reach 12
notes: No mainstem road crossings. This reach is the identified upper limit of anadromous (chinook) access.

habitat_value: Spawning minimal (large bed material, no adult holding pools, possible migration barriers in Reach 12); rearing may be moderate for bull trout (abundant cobble riffle), limited by absence of pool habitat and low debris.
upstream_fish: Bull trout sampled (Reach 13); rainbow present (mainstem up to Reach 14)
recommendation: Re-plant cleared riparian areas in Reaches 11 & 13 (Sec 6.5, low/medium restoration priority)
notes: Nugget Gulch Creek enters the east bank at the upper reach boundary. Two unnamed tributaries on west side. Branch logging road crosses mainstem ~350 m below upper boundary.

habitat_value: No significant spawning (large cobble bed, low pool frequency, possible upstream migration barriers in Reach 12); low to moderate rearing (cobble riffle + some side channel).
upstream_fish: Bull trout sampled (Reach 14); rainbow trout - mainstem upper limit up to Reach 14, may extend further
notes: One major debris jam caused a high-velocity cascade but 'did not appear to obstruct upstream fish passage'. Sawflat Creek confluence; mainline logging road crosses mainstem in upper section.

habitat_value: Moderate spawning for resident and anadromous fish (limited by low holding pools, high fines); moderate to high rearing (abundant side-channel habitat, organic debris and cobble cover).
upstream_fish: Chinook spawning documented in lower reach of Pleasant Valley/Antler tributaries; unconfirmed chinook spawning may occur in lower Summit Creek; bull trout in lower reaches
recommendation: Stabilize upstream sediment sources (high sand content - high); create scour pools (low pool frequency - medium) (Sec 6.5)
notes: Tributary to Antler Creek (enters at upstream boundary of Antler Reach 2). Reaches 2-6 not assessed due to their low priority ratings.

habitat_value: No significant spawning or rearing capability due to highly unstable channel caused by ongoing placer mining operations; very little instream cover, low diversity, high fines.
notes: Highly disturbed channel; mining has destabilized the entire floodplain width in the upper portion of the reach.

habitat_value: No spawning or rearing habitat capability due to highly unstable channel caused by active placer mining; very little instream cover, low diversity, high fines.
notes: Reach only 300 m long (44 m riffle + 256 m glide/pool). LWD absent.

habitat_value: Spawning severely limited (high sand in bed material, absence of holding pools); rearing limited by low habitat diversity and lack of pool habitat/instream cover.
upstream_fish: Spawning chinook salmon observed in Reach 1; bull trout in lower reaches
recommendation: Stabilize upstream sediment sources if possible (specialist required) (Sec 6.5)
notes: 2nd-order tributary to Antler Creek (enters lower Reach 7). Lower reach heavily influenced by outwash deposits from Grouse Creek.

barrier: A 1.5 m high rock chute in Reach 2 likely impedes upstream fish passage to all species in this system (Executive Summary describes it as a possible fish migration barrier - 2-3 m falls)
recommendation: If significant chinook spawning capability is found upstream of this barrier, the feasibility of removing the barrier should be examined (Executive Summary)
notes: Reach 2 moderately confined by valley walls; not assessed in detail (only Reach 1 assessed).

barrier: Three rock chutes with gradients of 9 to 21% occupy 9% of the Reach 1 channel length
habitat_value: Spawning severely limited (unstable channel, absence of pool holding habitat); rearing constrained (unstable channel, no off-channel); high-gradient cobble/boulder habitats in upper section provide moderate rearing for resident rainbow and bull trout.
upstream_fish: Spawning chinook reported in lower Grouse Creek; juvenile chinook rearing confirmed in lower reach; bull trout in lower reaches; rainbow/bull trout upper section
recommendation: No restoration work identified - high lateral channel instability (Sec 6.5, priority = NA)
notes: Tributary to Pleasant Valley Creek. North valley wall highly unstable, actively sliding into the channel over ~900 m (lower slump 300 m long, max 40 m high).

habitat_value: No significant spawning (large bed material, aggrading channel); marginal rearing (low diversity, absence of pool habitat, low debris); shallow depths suggest not suitable for overwintering juvenile fish.
upstream_fish: Bull trout found in lower reaches of Nugget Gulch Creek (per Antler Creek fish distribution)
recommendation: Stabilize erosion at mine sites (high); habitat-diversity work requires stabilization first (low) (Sec 6.5)
notes: 2nd-order tributary of Antler Creek, flows NE into Antler Creek at upstream boundary of Antler Reach 13. Severely impacted by past placer mining and eroding tailings/access road; highly turbid (~5 cm visibility).

barrier: Immediately upstream of the Reach 2 boundary the channel is a high-gradient (25%) cascade/chute with a boulder bed material
habitat_value: Continuous riffle/cascade with no pool or glide areas; large cobble/gravel bed. Severely impacted by past placer mining.
notes: Reach 2 is 0.3 km long, average channel gradient 10%.

habitat_value: Moderate to high spawning for resident and anadromous fish (gravel availability, holding pools and fish access rated 'good'; gravel quality 'fair' due to high sands); moderate rearing (abundant functional LWD, undercut banks, side channels), limited by low cobble cover ('poor') and pool areas ('poor').
upstream_fish: Fish access rated 'good' (resident and anadromous fish)
recommendation: Install tree revetments (hand fall) for low pool frequency; identify and stabilize sediment sources for poor gravel quality (Sec 6.5)
notes: One major logjam near upper boundary caused channel braiding but 'did not appear to impede fish passage'. High sands suspected related to past logging in upper watershed (incl. Ketcham Creek).

habitat_value: Moderate to high spawning for resident and anadromous fish (gravel availability, holding pools and fish access rated 'good'; gravel quality 'fair' due to high sands); moderate rearing (abundant functional LWD, undercut banks, side channels), limited by low cobble cover ('poor') and pool areas ('poor').
upstream_fish: Fish access rated 'good' (resident and anadromous fish); good fish access to all off-channel habitats
recommendation: Install boulder groups for low pool frequency; identify and stabilize sediment sources for poor gravel quality (Sec 6.5)
notes: Tributary to West Creek. Mainstem bridge crossing present; logjam ~0.7 km upstream of the mainstem bridge created multiple channels. Several beaver dams/ponds in upper reach.

barrier: Upstream boundary of Reach 1 defined by a series of waterfalls cascading over a vertical distance of 12 m; anadromous fish access limited to the lower 1.2 km downstream of this 12 m high cascading waterfall (impassable; not feasible to remove)
habitat_value: Moderate spawning for resident and anadromous fish (no fish-access limitations within Reach 1; holding pools and spawning gravel abundant/'good', low scour; limited by high sand - 'fair'); moderate rearing (good functional debris + side channels; limited by low pool frequency - 'poor').
upstream_fish: Chinook salmon, rainbow trout and bull trout documented in lower creek; non-salmonids mountain whitefish and sculpin present. Anadromous access limited to lower 1.2 km (below the 12 m falls).
recommendation: Install tree revetments (hand fall) for low pool frequency; install/stabilize sediment sources for poor gravel quality (Sec 6.5)
notes: Reach 1 is 1.5 km from Bowron River confluence up to the falls. High sands suspected related to past logging in upper watershed. Logjam in upper section did not impede fish passage.

stream_name: Unnamed tributary to Reach 2 of Victoria Creek mainstem

recommendation: Bank stabilization; substantial disturbed/eroding banks from mining are a sediment source

recommendation: No action; no significant disturbance found

habitat_value: Channel type: Step-Pool boulder/wood; Condition: Stable
notes: Stop 1: ~200 m upstream of confluence with Cariboo River. Control: Boulders and gradient; Banks: Boulder and LWD, stable. Disturbance indicators: None. Comment: LWD very sparse, providing little control; channel constriction from adjacent road; hill slopes coupled; Spanish Lake acting as sediment buffer. Riparian land use: Placer adjacent to lower mainstem; conditions: mature mixed wood forest with potential recruitable LWD; riparian reserve of at least one channel width seems acceptable. Photos C3, C4.

habitat_value: Channel type: Riffle-pool cobble/gravel/wood; Condition: Slightly aggraded, but stable
notes: Stop 2: ~200 m upstream of Blackbear main crossing. Control: LWD; Banks: Stable fluvial deposits. Disturbance: None. Comment: Bed load sand/gravel; LWD providing pool and bank cover; slopes partially coupled. Riparian land use: None; conditions: low shrub-grass with conifers, roots providing bank stability; riparian conditions appear natural, buffer of at least three channel widths should be left intact. Photos C5, C6.

habitat_value: Channel type: Step-pool boulder/wood; Condition: Slightly aggraded, but stable

habitat_value: Channel type: Riffle-pool gravel/wood; Condition: Moderately aggraded
notes: Stop 4: Middle Blackbear Creek. Control: Gradient; Banks: Well rounded materials. Disturbance: (S3) Sediment wedges, (B2) Eroding banks, (B3) Avulsions, (C3) Elevated mid-channel bars. Comment: LWD exists but not providing much control; hill slopes partially coupled; high bed load of shale and slate from surrounding hill slopes. Riparian land use: None at this site; conditions: mature forest and shrub; perhaps placer upstream delivering sediment to channel. Photos SP9, SP10.

habitat_value: Channel type: Cascade-pool boulder/wood; Condition: Slightly aggraded

habitat_value: Channel type: Cascade-pool cobble/wood; Condition: Slightly aggraded
notes: Stop 1: Keithley Creek at upper Keithley mainline crossing. Control: Boulder, bedrock and LWD control; Banks: Stable. Disturbance: None. habitat_value: Channel type: Cascade-pool cobble; Condition: Slightly degraded

habitat_value: Channel type: Riffle-pool cobble/wood; Condition: Moderately aggraded

habitat_value: Channel type: Cascade-pool cobble; Condition: Slightly aggraded

habitat_value: Channel type: Step-pool boulder/wood; Condition: Stable
notes: Stop 1: Below pulled bridge crossing. Control: Boulder and rock; Banks: Appear stable. Disturbance: None. habitat_value: Channel type: Step-pool boulder/wood; Condition: Stable
notes: Stop 3: Harveys mainline at Harveys Creek crossing. Control: Boulder and rock; Banks: No instability noted. Disturbance: None. Comment: Road surface and ditch erosion is a concern. notes: Stop 4: Harveys Creek alluvial fan. Control: Gradient; Banks: Unstable. Disturbance: (B2) Eroding banks, (C4) Multiple channels or braids, (D2) LWD oriented parallel to channel. habitat_value: Channel type: Cascade-pool boulder; Condition: Stable
notes: Stop 1: ~50 m upstream of road crossing. Control: Gradient; Banks: Stable. Disturbance: None. habitat_value: Channel type: Cascade-pool boulder; Condition: Stable
notes: Stop 2: ~50 m upstream of Maeford Lake main. Control: Bedrock and boulder; Banks: No instability noted. Disturbance: None. habitat_value: Channel type: Riffle-pool gravel; Condition: Aggraded
notes: Stop 4: Little River at G road crossing. Control: Gradient; Banks: Eroding, unstable gravel, silt and sand. Disturbance: (B2) Eroding banks. habitat_value: Channel type: Riffle-pool cobble; Condition: Moderately aggraded

habitat_value: Channel type: Cascade-pool cobble/wood; Condition: Slightly aggraded

habitat_value: Channel type: Step-pool boulder/wood; Condition: Stable
notes: Stop 4: PHOTO SITE ONLY. Riparian land use: Harvested to one bank. Photo C8.

habitat_value: Channel type: Riffle-pool sand/wood; Condition: Slightly aggraded

barrier: Culvert crossing on lower Ramsay Creek - local residents attempting to have it replaced with a bridge to ensure fish access is maintained to upper reaches. A beaver dam ~2 km upstream (identified by Rosberg 1975 as a potential barrier) was breached when observed in 1987 and posed no difficulty for spawners. New logging road developments in upper creek causing siltation at a bridge crossing site.
habitat_value: Excellent spawning gravels, good low summer flows, impressive fry numbers; very important spawning and rearing stream. ~12% of Francois Lake fry and just under 2% of parr production.
upstream_fish: Yes - nearly 9 km accessible to fish from Francois Lake; rainbow trout only species captured
recommendation: Highest priority habitat protection; fencing to keep cattle out of lower creek; residents seek replacement of culvert crossing with a bridge; advise Ministry of Forests/Lands and Ministry of Highways of the creek's importance. Enhancement/protection priority #5.
notes: Sample sites R1, R2. Watershed 43.2 km2.

habitat_value: Completely dewatered during August; did not contribute significantly to rainbow production in 1987.
notes: No sampling attempted (dewatered).

barrier: No barriers noted; drains Francois Lake into Fraser Lake. Log drives conducted 1914 to as recently as 1965.
